title: oasis: animals at world creation, respawn event, combat animal stats
criteria:
Add wild animals to oases (T23 part a). Config already exists: `cfg.oasis` (OasisSection: bonus, radius, max_per_village, respawn_hours, respawn_fraction, animals: dict[str, AnimalDef(name_th, def_inf, def_cav, min, max)]) and EventType.OASIS_RESPAWN. EDITING RULE: realm/services/worlds.py, realm/core/worldgen.py, realm/core/combat.py and realm/engine/handlers.py already exist and hold proofread text: change them ONLY with small targeted Edit operations (no whole-file rewrites).
== realm/core/worldgen.py ==
Add `oasis_animals(seed: int, x: int, y: int, cfg) -> dict[str, int]`: rng = random.Random(f'{seed}:oasis:{x}:{y}'); for each animal key of cfg.oasis.animals (YAML order) count = rng.randint(animal.min, animal.max); returns {key: count}. Pure and deterministic.
== realm/core/combat.py ==
`ArmyGroup` gets a new last field `stats: dict[str, tuple[float, float]] | None = None` (unit key -> (def_inf, def_cav)). In the defense sum, a group with stats not None uses stats[unit] directly (ignoring tribe multipliers and upgrades, for every unit with count > 0); other groups behave as before. Animals never attack.
== realm/services/worlds.py ==
(1) In create_world: the bulk-inserted tile rows of oasis tiles (kind 'oasis') get `'animals': worldgen.oasis_animals(seed, x, y, cfg)`; other kinds get no animals (None). (2) After ROUND_END is scheduled also schedule the first OASIS_RESPAWN: events.schedule(s, world.id, EventType.OASIS_RESPAWN, game_epoch + timedelta(seconds=cfg.oasis.respawn_hours * 3600 / speed), {}). (3) Append `respawn_oases(s, world_id, now, cfg) -> None`: world = s.get(World, world_id); None or status != 'running' -> return; for every Tile of the world with kind 'oasis' and oasis_owner_village_id IS NULL: target = worldgen.oasis_animals(world.seed, tile.x, tile.y, cfg); current = tile.animals or {}; new = {key: min(target[key], current.get(key, 0) + math.ceil(target[key] * cfg.oasis.respawn_fraction)) for key in target}; assign `tile.animals = new` only when it differs from current; finally schedule the next OASIS_RESPAWN at now + timedelta(seconds=cfg.oasis.respawn_hours * 3600 / world.speed) with payload {}; flush.
== realm/engine/handlers.py ==
Add `handle_oasis_respawn(s, ev, cfg)` calling worlds.respawn_oases(s, ev.world_id, ev.due_at, cfg) and register it in HANDLERS under EventType.OASIS_RESPAWN (all other entries unchanged).
== Tests ==
tests/core/test_oasis.py (pure): oasis_animals is deterministic (same args -> same dict; different coordinates usually differ), has exactly the keys rat, spider, boar, every count within [min, max] of the config (rat 8..20, spider 4..12, boar 2..8), over 200 sample coordinates each key reaches both its min and its max range region (at least one value <= min+2 and one >= max-2); combat with stats: 10 'rat' with stats {'rat': (25, 20)} defending (ArmyGroup(tribe='stonehold', units={'rat': 10}, stats={'rat': (25.0, 20.0)})) against 30 swordsmen of 'ironwild' (ATTACK, wall 0, defender_tribe 'stonehold'): attack_power == 1200.0, defense_power == 10*25 + 10 = 260.0 (all attackers are infantry so only def_inf counts), attacker_won True, defender_losses == [{'rat': 10}] (all die), attacker_losses == {'swordsman': 3} (x = (260/1200)**1.5 = 0.10086 -> int(30*0.10086 + 0.5) = 3); with 20 swordsmen instead (A = 800): defense 260 -> still attacker wins with int(20*(260/800)**1.5+0.5) = int(20*0.18529+0.5) = 4 losses; a normal group (stats None) behaves exactly as before.
tests/services/test_oasis_respawn.py (DB fixtures `s`, `cfg`, `t0`; world = worlds.create_world(s, seed=1, speed=1, player_name='ผู้เล่น', tribe='stonehold', bot_count=0, cfg=cfg, real_now=t0)): every oasis tile of the world has animals equal to worldgen.oasis_animals(1, x, y, cfg) and every non-oasis tile has animals None; there is exactly one pending OASIS_RESPAWN event due at epoch + 43200 s (12 h at speed 1) with payload {}; in a speed 10 world (own test) it is due at epoch + 4320 s; respawn: set one oasis tile's animals to {} -> worlds.respawn_oases(s, world.id, t0 + 43200 s, cfg) gives each animal exactly min(target, ceil(target * 0.25)) and a second call gives min(target, 2 * ceil(target * 0.25)) (compute with math.ceil from the target dict in the test); a tile already at full target is unchanged; an oasis with oasis_owner_village_id set (use the human village id) is NOT touched; the call schedules the next OASIS_RESPAWN 12 h after the given now; process_next through the engine (realm.engine.worker.process_next(s, world, epoch + 43200 s, cfg)) runs the handler, the event ends 'done' and a new pending OASIS_RESPAWN exists.
notes:
- No Thai text is needed in this task; do not touch any Thai string in the existing files.
- Tile columns: kind (str 'oasis'), oasis_type, oasis_owner_village_id, animals (JSONB). Use real columns only in tests.
- Existing tests must keep passing; tests that count scheduled events for a fresh world may need the extra OASIS_RESPAWN event accounted for: if an existing assertion breaks only because of this new event (e.g. 'exactly 1 event'), you MAY adjust that single assertion minimally in the affected test file (list the file in docs/handoff).
- Never commit; never call datetime.now().
